I retired three years ago, and I am not going to waste a single summer. Next June, my brother and I are chartering a boat in Greece. The flights are booked, the marina is booked, and we are leaving Lisbon on the second of June. I have a full itinerary on my kitchen wall. Every island, every harbor, every restaurant. My wife laughs at me. She says the wind will change my plans on the first day, and she is probably right. But I like to look forward to a trip for months. Half the fun is the planning. This time next summer, I will be sailing between two Greek islands with a cold drink in my hand. And when the wind changes, I will make a new plan. That is what plans are for.

People always ask me where I am going next, and I never have an answer. I do not make plans. I think a full itinerary kills a trip. Next month I am flying to Buenos Aires, and that is the only thing I have booked. No hotel, no list, nothing. I will probably take a bus to the south, but who knows? Last year I met a family on a day trip in Chile, and they invited me to their farm for a week. That would never happen with a plan. My son thinks I am crazy. He says that one day I am going to get stuck somewhere with no bed. Maybe. But this time next month, I will be walking somewhere I have never heard of, and I will be happy.
